_note: Dollar settings for scoring/economics.js. Crop yields and prices are NOT here: they come from each field's real USDA NASS data (field.market.recent, 2021-2025). NASS Quick Stats has no fertilizer price series for Texas, so the nitrogen price comes from the USDA AMS Illinois Production Cost Report: a national estimate, not Texas.
_nPriceMath: USDA AMS Illinois Production Cost Report (Bi-weekly), Nov 13, 2026, distributor ask averages. Anhydrous ammonia 82-0-0: $981.11/ton / (2000 lb x 0.82 = 1640 lb N) = $0.598/lb N -> 0.60 (used: cheapest N per lb, so the legume nitrogen credit is not overstated). For comparison: urea 46-0-0 $770.00/ton / 920 lb N = $0.837/lb N; UAN 28% $467.86/ton / 560 lb N = $0.835/lb N.

nPriceSource.dataset: USDA AMS Illinois Production Cost Report
nPriceSource.report: USDA AMS Illinois Production Cost Report (Bi-weekly), report 3195

nCreditSource: Cover crops don't hand over all the nitrogen they fix to the next crop. We count half (planning rule of thumb, still to be checked with AgriLife / NRCS).
